top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn for the Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes demand-estimation core. Its credit set maps onto one jointly authored contribution, so attribution is clean once the citation is limited to demand and competition in differentiated-product markets. The work made substitution patterns, market power, merger effects and welfare measurable from market data with endogenous prices, so it changed what can be credibly known. About three decades of use in merger review, antitrust, regulation, trade, health and environmental analysis, together with critique and refinement, give a record of maturity. No member has raised an overlap with a prior prize. The main reservations are that it is a methods prize without a headline finding, that estimates are sensitive to instruments and functional form, and that the three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin. I judge these answerable with narrow, method-focused wording. I rely on colleagues' statements for the use and validation record and have not verified it independently. P002 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn) is a credible design-based prize with a clean trio, but its persistence, magnitude and shift-share debates make it less mature, so I rank it second. Both are preferable to no award (P000).
